notes: Access: curl_cffi chrome124 browser impersonation past the site's Cloudflare JS challenge. robots.txt checked, no Claude-specific disallow, but disallows /s/ (search) and /h/ (individual PDP offer pages) for all agents -- neither was fetched; the listing page itself, /hs/, is NOT under either disallowed prefix ('/hs/' != '/h/'). Checked homepage, footer nav ('Filialen und Standorte' section), sitemap-categories.xml (3098 URLs, no dedicated abverkauf/raeumung/restposten/outlet-named category node -- unlike sister site XXXLutz DE/SR105 which had a dedicated 'Abverkauf' hub with 22 category children, moemax.de has NO equivalent multi-child clearance hub in its category tree), sitemap-cms.xml (547 CMS pages) scanned for sale/abverkauf/outlet/raeumung/restposten-named pages. INCLUDED: /hs/ ('Filialschnaeppchen' = 'Branch/Store Bargains'), reached via a footer-nav link under 'Filialen und Standorte' (Branches & Locations) and also linked from the /c/sale page ('Kuechen-Abverkauf in deiner Naehe!' -> /hs/?p_livingarea=Kueche, a facet re-cut of the same listing, not a separate category per the established non-canonical-facet-variant rule from the prior Home-Decor pass). Verified as a genuine PLP: SSR JSON pagination block {pageSize:60, totalPages:18, totalResults:1041} plus matching rendered resultCountContainer data-track-value="1041"; exhaustion check ceil(1041/60)=17.35->18 matches totalPages=18. Product tiles inspected: each item is data-product-id='offer_<id>' (an 'offer' record distinct from normal catalog SKUs), links to /h/moemax-<slug>-offer_<id> (individually priced, one-off), and is tagged with a specific physical branch (e.g. 'moemax Dresden') under the price -- confirming these are single-piece, store-tied bargain/liquidation items (floor models / discontinued individual pieces sold below list price at a named branch), which is the functional equivalent of an outlet/clearance concept even though the site's own label is 'Filialschnaeppchen' rather than a literal 'clearance' word. Classified as Clearance (not Sale) because: it is a permanent structural site section (footer-nav category, present in the SPA's persistent navigation, not a dated campaign), lists individually-priced liquidation stock rather than a percent-off promotion across the regular catalogue, and is tied to physical-store disposal of floor/discontinued stock -- matching the brief's 'End of Line'/outlet-style merchandising test more than a temporary promotional Sale. EXCLUDED as generic temporary Sale (not Clearance), per Sec.3's Sale-vs-Clearance test: (1) /c/sale ('% SALE bei moemax %' / 'Moebel Sale online bis -70%') -- editorial/campaign landing page (headings like 'Moebel Sale: Zuschnappen beim moemax Sale!', '3 Tipps fuer die Schnaeppchen-Tour'), its own 'Alle SALE-Artikel' link points to /s/?...p_pricepromotionid=MM781-MM795 (a dated price-promotion ID encoded in the URL = temporary campcampaign, also robots-disallowed and itself a search-results/filter page, doubly excluded). Its body copy explains general reasons prices are sometimes lower (mentions Restposten/Outlet/Lagerraeumung as concepts) but the page itself is promotional copy, not a clearance listing. (2) /c/lagersale ('Lagersale Moebel - Jetzt guenstige Artikel bei moemax entdecken') -- confirmed via embedded CMS JSON to be cmsPageTypeSubtype='shopTheLooks', i.e. an image-tile grid landing page whose links go to plain, unfiltered category pages (e.g. /alle-teppiche-fussmatten-C32) with no sale/clearance facet applied -- not a listing of its own. (3) Seasonal promo pages found by name pattern in sitemap-cms.xml (/c/winter-sale, /c/summer-sale, /c/blackfriday, /c/deals, /c/eiskalte-schnaeppchen, /c/badezimmer-sale, /c/arbeitszimmer-sale, /c/wohnzimmer-sale, /c/schlafzimmer-sale) were spot-checked (3 of them) and each now returns the SPA's empty content-shell (~4.3KB, no CMS content resolved) -- consistent with expired/inactive seasonal campaigns, not permanent clearance pages; not individually re-fetched beyond the spot check given the clear pattern. No ambiguous cases requiring a MANUAL REVIEW flag -- the Sale-vs-Clearance distinction was clear cut in every case examined.
